title: Acceptance implies proximity to the property
statement: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet, let $n\\ge1$, and let $V$ be a probabilistically checkable proof of proximity system on words of length $n$, with proof length $\\ell$ and a positive soundness rate $r$. Let $P$ be a property of length-$n$ words, and suppose $V$ has perfect completeness and rejects every word whose relative Hamming distance from every word satisfying $P$ is greater than any given $\\delta\\in[0,1]$ with probability strictly greater than $r\\delta$. If a word $w$ and proof cause $V$ to accept with probability at least $1-r\\varepsilon$ for some $\\varepsilon\\in[0,1]$, then there is a word satisfying $P$ at relative Hamming distance at most $\\varepsilon$ from $w$.
hypotheses_covered: The alphabet is finite and has decidable equality
$V$ is a PCPP system with input length $n$ and some proof length and query bound
$V$ satisfies the PCPP conditions for property $P$ and rate $r$
An input word and proof have acceptance probability at least $1-r\\varepsilon$
